newsitem.title: USA: Advanta launches card tied to AmEx rewards.
newsitem.headline: Advanta launches card tied to AmEx rewards.

text.p: Advanta Corp. is teaming up with American Express Co. to provide a new no-fee credit card that gives users points that can be used for cash discounts at participating merchants, the companies said Thursday.
Advanta, a Spring House, Pa.-based consumer finance company, will issue MasterCard or Visa credit cards that will be linked to American Express's Membership Rewards programme.
An American Express spokesman said it is the first such card alliance between American Express and another card issuer in the United States.

The companies said the Rewards Accelerator Card, issued by Advanta National Bank will have an 8.9 percent introductory rate for six months. Thereafter, the interest rate for purchases and balance transfers becomes the prime rate plus 9.65 percent, currently 17.9 percent.

Customers who use the new card will earn one Membership Rewards point for every $10 of their total month-end balance, which includes new purchases, cash advances and balance transfers, plus any balance carried over from the previous month.

Customers who transfer $500 or more from other credit cards to Rewards Accelerator will receive 1,000 bonus points at the time of acquiring the card. Rewards Accelerator cardholders earn points if they become or remain American Express cardmembers enrolled in Membership Rewards.

Harvy Golub, chairman and chief executive of American Express, noted in a statement that the average U.S. consumer uses six separate credit cards. "This new card will leverage the power of Membership Rewards, help Advanta capture business that has been going to other issuers and provide financial benefits to both of us," he said.
The Visa credit card association responded that it is concerned about "the arrangement's potential negative effect on intersystem competition."
For American Express, the alliance represents its entry into the U.S. bank card business, but falls short of its objective of forming alliances in which U.S. banks would issue American Express cards.

Moshe Orenbuch, an analyst with Sanford C. Bernstein Co., said if the Rewards Accelerator card is successful it could help American Express in its efforts get the Visa and MasterCard U.S. bylaws changed. He said because Advanta now has an exclusive deal with American Express other banks could become more willing to cooperate with American Express if they think they can get something in return.

In a telephone press conference, Advanta Chief Executive Officer Alex "Pete" Hart said the first wave of solicitations for the new cards went into the mail Wednesday night but he declined to say how big the mailing was or how many people the companies expect to sign up for the new card.
Advanta is the ninth-largest U.S. credit card company based on $12.7 billion in outstanding receivables at the end of the third quarter.
